chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin'an who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

God, the Mighty and Majestic, has received a pledge from the believer so that his speech is not accepted, his narration is not believed, he does not take revenge from his enemy, and he does not satisfy his anger except by exposing himself, because every believer is silent.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the believer being 'muzzled' (maljum) in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this *mithaq* as a defining trait of the *Awliya* (friends of God), where self-effacement (*khud*) serves as the antidote to ego-driven conflict. The term *miljam* (muzzled) signifies a believer who restrains their tongue from exposing others' faults, thereby preserving social harmony and spiritual purity. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on *hilm* (forbearance) and the internalization of accountability rather than external judgment.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-69 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “

God has received a pledge from the believer so that his speech doesn’t become accepted, they do not believe his narration, he doesn’t take revenge from his enemy unless he divulges himself because every believer is silent.”
